Desire to Follow Community Guidelines: If my actions were unintentionally perceived as smurfing, I’d like to better understand how I can adjust my behavior to avoid these misunderstandings. I want to continue playing within the game’s rules, as I am genuinely passionate about Dota 2.

Is there a possibility of reviewing this ban in light of the context provided?
I appreciate any assistance you can offer, as my goal is to continue enjoying and supporting Dota 2 while adhering to all rules. I hope this information clarifies my intentions and circumstances. Thank you for your time and support.

Gettign punished for "overwatch penalties" when there has been no actual time to review. This I beleive is a false positive of whatever the hell the devs are doing to auto send palyers to LP

30 positive matches with 0 reports, literally the match right after my conduct update. Somehow on a game where there are 2 griefers IM THE ONE THAT ENDS UP PUNISHED. Screenshots below

Match ID 7987252157

Clearly axe offlane and mid alchemist wanted nothing to do with the game past minute 5, went out of their way to avoid fights and jungled after losing their lanes. they went 0-5 0-2. I reported both of them 

To my surprise IM THE ONE THAT ENDED UP IN LP, all for one match without any previous reports. 

Seriously fix your dumb system, Im trying to recalibrate and every game is a skill imbalanced or a griefing shitshow.

But banning me for 24 hours and sendign me to LP cuz a weekend player decided it would be cute to report me is unacceptable despite that me and the other support were the ones still trying.

Worse than that, lying to the player and saying this is "an overwatch conviction" and not a >report threshold Is unacceptable. There is no way this could've been an overwatch conviction if there was no time for the replay to even be ready for review. 

LP on 1 game when I have 0 record of reports or abandons in the past 30 matches is unacceptable. 

At some point you have to realize many factors affect reports. If its a loss, more people report, if its a weekend, more people report, if the person uses chat and doesnt grief, he is more likely to get reported wrongly, if its a stomp because of diff in skill or cuz someone griefed, more reports get dashed out all around aside from the griefer. The insulting part here is the actual griefers didnt get punished. 

Enough is enough, Valve fix your shit, you've had 12 years. Your current players will continue to tank, no amount of events will help recover them if you dont give people incentives to actually behave, and implement a system that actually works.

Description

Behavior score currently matters more than skill ranking on game quality experience and it probably will be the cause for many players to stop once the novelty of updates wears off.

**The report is both underutilized and abused.** My guess is most people dont actually bother reporting, they either dont know the options exist or its not intuitive to get to that page. Why do I say this? because 2-3 reports from 2 parties can land you in LP with NO OVERWATCH ASSESSMENT (the assessment occurs before the replay is even available for download). Think about that, out of 135 players you encounter in 15 matches that could report you,  2-3 reports is not even 2%. Not to mention Im talking from experience in TURBO mode, not ranked, not even casual AP.  
Suggestion#1: If commend worth was decreased to prevent players form boosting BS through turbo, then also adjust the weight of reports, particularly when it comes to dashing out punishment. Currently a conduct update with 30+ commend and reports nets around 150-180 BS. So if a player DCs or abandons you are telling that player that they need to play ~100 games to recover. That to me does not seem balanced at all. (I have no doubts overwatch eventually will be partly AI powered, it needs to a account when losses are simply stomps, and I cant emphasize this enough, an ability draft or turbo game is much different than All pick or ranked, they cant be treated the same)
Suggestion#2: Baselines for behavior should be aligned with average BS, lower BS players tend to be a lot more trigger happy with report use, while top BS players might not bother reporting at all. The same behavior in a lower BS match can net you reports you wouldn't get at high BS. Since you are allowing players with questionable behavior to make the call I think its only fair that their report is curved appropriately. 

**Reports are not being used correctly,** from overwatch reviews about 50% of them I see no griefing behavior, people report players they dont like more often than behavior that should be punished, and the way devs have limited this is to give each player limited reports. Also this affects new players, Ive had several friends I tried to introduce to the game get reported for griefing when they were just learning the game. Losing or getting stomped or even underperforming are not valid reasons to be called a griefer or get reported, the system currently takes no account of this
**Suggestion#3:** Make reports actually be submitted at the END of the match, when people have cooler heads, when players that quit 3 minutes before the game ends have already closed the game. This prevents people from assessing what went on in the match entirely instead of an instance of someone rage buying back, or a player with a unconventional pick or build. They can still flag instances of behavior during the match, although since about a year ago you can no longer report a player multiple times a match to flag when they were being toxic, so I am guessing the devs saw no value in this
**Suggestion#4:** Instead of giving the option to a player to click every single box in the report page, make players select a single reason per report through a tickbox or dropdown menu UI. Lists what constitutes and what does not constitute griefing, comm abuse, hacking, scripting, etc. CS2, Apex, overwatch and many other online comp games use this

players that actively engage in repeat griefing should not be able to report. I would even say it doesnt make sense for a player that went 0-35 feeding mid in a game to have the power to report anyone else in that game, and I can confirm Ive been at the receiving end of this. 
**Suggestion#5:** Dont allow repeat offenders to use reports, even retroacrtively remove reports they have submitted if they are found guilty of bad behavior in the same match. These players would need a clear statement of the consequence to their actions. Give them feedback that they temporarily lose the ability to call out other players behavior because of their own. 
**Suggestion#6:** Immortal behavior is probably at its worst with the current drafting system. It seems to give a pass to players to be toxic because they are at the top 5% of rank jsut so that queue times arent as long.  All this is doing is encouraging players to purchase alt accounts to play in or resort to boosting services. Make example of players, example, Mason

https://www.reddit.com/r/DotA2/comments/17voh09/masondota2_paid_for_is_currently_being_behavior/


Ona final note, If the goal of the devs is to get people in a treadmill run of BS farming, you will lose player base once the novelty of updates wear off. What keeps dota players coming back and not quitting is match quality. The suggestions  I put forward go along with the current system, I think a much bigger overhaul (like allowing infinite reports like in CS and re-baselining automatic punishment) and simplifying the system would only improve player experience, but at least are small things that could help. I hope some attention is brought on this matter

(22.03.2024)
I don’t know English, and I will translate from Russian into English through a translator, I apologize in advance for strange sentences

I received 5 punishments from Patrol over the last 8-12 days, here is my ID - 243935559, dotabuff is open

I would like to ask the Dota developers, in which match did I receive my last punishment? Not after what did I receive punishment from the Patrol, but precisely for what match did I receive punishment?
I fundamentally disagree with the punishment, for the last 8 games I have not violated it in order to get another block for 24 hours and games in “low priority”
I think the Dota developers decided that the Patrol itself would decide who to block and who not, without checking with the developers themselves

I am a player of 5-4 positions, I play at a high rank, and I think because in this role you can perform very multifaceted actions that the patrol will not understand or will not consider “griefer”
For example, after the next block, I analyzed my last games and thought that the fact is that I like to “wander”, that is, I leave my line too often and early and leave my Carry or Troika alone for a long time, but at the same time I somehow I do that on other lanes, I control runs, I like to play mid and so on, but the patrol considers it a “violation”, and in the end I stopped doing it, because I thought that the problem was in my gameplay and what I like "wander", but in the end everything turned out to be wrong and after a while I again received a block from the Patrol
I don’t know what to do and how to understand why I continue to receive bans and most likely will continue to receive them, even in the last few games I did not play Dota itself and was thinking what should I do so that the patrol will think that I am not violating. But as you can see, it didn't help

Since I have been playing Dota for a long time and know what a violation is, I cannot understand where and in what place I was violated in the last “last” games (as it is written in the violation message), I would just be glad to see the match ID together with a violation message, because I can analyze the game and understand what the problem is, but I can’t
In the last game after which I received a block from the Patrol, I did not violate, but I rewatched this game and saw how my teammates, out of the blue, sent me reports due to a misunderstanding or their inattention, here is the ID of the last game - 7648930493. But even there there were no violations AT ALL and we even won.
On the contrary, opponents griefed, pressed moves behind their teammates and did not connect to fights that affected the game, and none of them received a ban (I checked the dotabuff, and it does not show up in “successful complaints”), but I received...

There are several topics  about micro-lags in the Ethernet([Like this one](https://steamcommunity.com/app/570/discussions/0/598198356167287325)) or [this one](https://dota2.ru/forum/threads/postojannye-mikro-frizy-v-dote-na-1-2-sekundy.1470915/). I have the same issue since a long while. 
I managed to change two PCs from the first time I faced it and this is my third one. Each time, it helped a bit. But the issue hasn't gone away.

I decided to solve this bug again today. I haven't solved it again. **But I managed to trigger it on purpose!** And I'm going to share my experience with You. I hope It will help You make the DOTA 2 gameplay process even better than it is now! 

My Pc Spec:

> Processor        13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13600KF, 3500 MHz, 14 Core(s), 14 Logical Processor(s)
> Installed RAM	32.0 GB (31.8 GB usable)
> OS Name	        Microsoft Windows 11 Pro
> System type	64-bit operating system, x64-based processor
> Edition	        Windows 11 Pro
> OS build	        22621.3007

> BIOS                Version/Date	American Megatrends Inc. 1604, 12/15/2023
> SMBIOS           Version 3.5
> Motherboard  Asus PRIME Z790-P WIFI
> Video Card  	NVIDIA GeForce GT 1030
> Ram              Kingston FURY DDR5-5200 32768MB PC5-41600 (Kit of 2x16384) Beast AM5 Black (KF552C36BBEK2-32) 
>
> Hyper-V - VM Monitor Mode Extensions	                        Yes
> Hyper-V - Second Level Address Translation Extensions	Yes
> Hyper-V - Virtualization Enabled in Firmware                  	No
> Hyper-V - Data Execution Protection                                    	Yes
> 
> Mouse     Xtrfy M42 RGB USB White 
> Keyboard Xtrfy K4 TKL RGB Kailh Red USB White 
> Monitor  27 DELL UP2716DA (210-AXWI)

Dota 2 settings:
All graphic settings are lowest.
Windowed  1024x768
Vulcan(But DX11 also has so).

To trigger the essential lag, not a micro one. You have to decrease the amount  of cores  to 4. **The more cores You have, the less this lag lasts and feels**. And then start walking for a while in Demo Hero mode. Once every 30 seconds or a minute, it usually happens for a short while. Sometimes several times in a short time. 

[This is a video that  shows the issue, and how I managed to trigger it.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V5ydl3HvUpM)

I haven't done it on video, but to trigger the lag even more frequently, it may be useful to set a low priority on the process.

The thing is that I feel this effect even if I set high priority and ran as administrator, on all cores, and even with an AMD RX 560 or AMD RX 590 video card. With the same or Intel Core I7-8700K processor. And even if Hyper-V is on.  On 1920x1080 or even 2560x1440 resolution.  The difference is just in the length of the lag, and it's frequency. But any way is not smooth. Except for some very rare, once a blue moon, exceptions.

If You need some additional information, I'm ready to give it. I hope You'll solve it, or help me understand where is the mistake if it is my mistake. Thank You in advance.

Description

My communication score is stuck at 5935. I've had 30 matches after the conduct summary that initially set it to 5935, i.e I've had 2 conduct summary updates after the initial one that set it to 5935. It was stuck at 5935 in both those updates.
I know for sure that I didn't get reported by anybody in those 30 matches as I was at my best behaviour and never got flamed by teammates or enemies. Those 30 matches included a all pick ranked games and turbo games.

I believe once the communication score gets below 6k, it can never increase. However, I believe it can decrease if reported for toxic chat/voice as there are players with lower behaviour score than 5k.
Maybe the inclusion of turbo matches bugs out the calculation? I haven't tested 15 matches in a row without turbo myself to know for sure, and neither will I. Just going to take a break from dota till this gets fixed.

What makes matters worse is that you can't even chat in party chat when you're below 6k. I'm sure that wasn't intended either.

Keep in mind my other "normal" behaviour score is 12k and I was ALWAYS high behaviour score in 10 years of playing dota.

after it dropped to around 8k I stopped using any form of communication and it still went down; currently cruising at 6800 and the last 1200-ish points were lost being fully muted and not abusing the system in any way. I do not report often, I don't grief game, I simply play dota. 2-3 more summaries and I will be unable to text completely. 

This is a serious issues, if it's a bug it should be fixed; if it's intentional it must be changed, this is not sustainable, I am not toxic and I do want to interact with my team to increase the odds of winning the game.

TLDR: I believe there must be some sort of integer error affecting the conduct summary and behavior score system. I provided data documenting my personal conduct summary numbers from Steam's Personal Game Data page.

Preamble: 
I have been playing Turbo mode in order to try to raise my behavior score. This failed miserably as evidenced by the current behavior score of 1. I have been punished by the Overwatch system multiple times with bans and low priority. I do not believe I have been acting in a way in game to warrant, especially in turbo games where it's supposed to be a casual mode for fun, and yet the amount of reports is insanely high from the players. Some of these conduct summaries were generated on the same day, either by actually playing 15 games in a day, or it auto-triggered and decreased score and gave me low priority. Again, I have been treating turbo games as a job, working to raise the score and have submitted requests to steam support about this. They have directed me to open a ticket here.

Request:
Please look at the data and see if there are any outstanding irregularities which would contribute to such a rapid decrease in score. 

I have a few questions to interpret from the data.
Why is there a negative integer? -34 and -67 reports
Why am i losing more score between summaries where more games were marked "positive" than not?
Why do i not gain score where there are 2 matches reported by 6 players compared to gaining score 27 reports by 12 players? These summaries are classified as Periodic and not Excessive Reports.
Is it statistically relevant to have so many commends and so many reports in the same conduct summary?
It has been a long-standing theory of mine that commends do not affect score, but if they are somehow not being counted then.
Are communication abuse reports being counted when below 3000 score and pings and voicelines are rate-limited to once every 60 seconds? Why? What about below 6000 score when you can use voicelines but not text chat? Is this counted as negative communication? What about below 7000 score, are multiple pings with a communication abuse report being triggered as a true positive? Why in God's name if yes?

I have included 4 screenshots that valve can decipher the Unix time of where patch 7.33 begins and where the change was made to the behavior score. It is my theory the system was reverted a few weeks after implementation, because people were. During this period, I personally had no complaints and thought my game quality was acceptable. I reached 5000 MMR for the first time during this period. I am currently banned from Ranked.

The screenshots are of the personal game data accessible on https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198384096495/gcpd/570/?category=Account&tab=MatchPlayerReportIncoming 
(For anyone reading this who would like to see their own game data, please replace my Steam user number in the link with your own. Follow Account -> Incoming Match Player Report.)
The column dates of course are organized from most recent to latest. 

I will be following the thread closely, please do add your thoughts if you have any comments about my data. Thank you.

### Example Match ID: 7423620413 

In the last turbo game I played before I was issued an automated 24 hour ban + at this time unknown number of low priority games, and a 1299 drop in behavior score to 1. I was matched with a party of 4, who took it upon themselves to grief and scapegoat me, as well as report me. I reported them and all 4 heros showed up as "action taken". It was easy to tell since I didn't report any other players. At 12 minutes Magnus wrote in the chat he was done. At around 15-16 min Magnus wasted RP in our fountain, used refresher, and wasted RP again.  The game was over at 17 min, but I believe we could have won if the party of 4 did not give up.
my dotabuff: https://www.dotabuff.com/players/423830767

### Screenshots
the ridiculously slow climb begins. I have been assessed a 24 hour ban and X games of low priority, as well as an instant reduction in 400 points after losing a game in which my teammates played less than average and exhibited toxic behavior. The automated system is a mistake, the report system is a mistake, trusting Valve gives a rat's ass about actual players is a mistake.

Description

Ever since the change to the behaviour score system, every game I play has been filled with toxic players who possess artificially inflated behaviour scores. The loading animation that plays immediately after the drafting phase always features a player who has received 120+ commends in the past few games, which is of course impossible unless every player on both teams is commending them after every game they play. Given that these individuals are often muted or proceed to conduct themselves in such a way as to warrant a mute or a handful of griefing reports, it is obvious that these players deserve low behaviour scores but are participating in some sort of lobby system in which the 9 other players in the lobby are commending them after each game. I'm not exactly sure how it works, but I can't think of any other explanation.

This has resulted in a far worse matchmaking experience than the one I had prior to the behaviour score change. I have a very high behaviour score, but my games are now filled with the sorts of toxic, game-ruining players I never had to play with under the old system. When I first read the changelogs, I thought the new system would be fantastic, and it certainly is on paper, but this artificial boosting needs to be fixed somehow so the changes can be positively felt as they were intended to be.

what a conduct summary currently looks like:
![image](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Dota2-Gameplay/assets/4257305/b9c1fd36-639c-4002-ad1d-2359dad2d2b6)

Here's the tooltip associated with the behavior score:
![image](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Dota2-Gameplay/assets/4257305/67e6c839-47dc-4e37-bd9d-941ea48d581f)

The problem (which I've seen people run into again and again) is that this screen implies two things it probably shouldn't:

1. The layout and lack of any explanatory text saying otherwise implies that behavior score is a direct function of the numbers shown below it and nothing else.
2. The tooltip reinforces this incorrect interpretation by implying that playing a match where you don't get reported is the one and only way to increase your behavior score.

Now, I don't have any kind of internal knowledge on how behavior scores are calculated, but from screenshots posted by people complaining I can clearly see that the two assumptions are both incorrect. Coupled with @vMcJohn's excellent GDC presentation about implementing VACnet for CS:GO, which didn't reveal the formula for Trust Factor, but did say that it is not solely based on a player's in-game actions. An example given in the presentation was that a player was complaining about cheaters in their matches and it turned out the player had 50 closely associated accounts that had been VAC banned.

I've seen people on the Dota 2 forum complaining that they created a smurf account and their behavior score followed them and even decreased further, so there's definitely something similar going on (or the behavior score system is just ridiculously good at guessing intent).

---

With all that said, my suggestion is a simple one: add one additional sentence to the conduct summary, reading:

> Your behavior score is not solely determined by the numbers on this doubt... the "Conduct Summary" tool does not work correctly on my Dota 2 account.

I have compared my "Conduct Summaries" with those of many colleagues in recent months, and most of them have worse summaries than mine. While they manage to reach a "Conduct" level of 10,000 and maintain it without many issues, mine keeps dropping and fluctuating, and for about a year now, I haven't come anywhere close to a "Conduct" score of 10,000.

It is true that I went through a phase where I complained about other people in chat, but that happened years ago. In the past few months, during which I've been conducting tests, I haven't even used the chat. I don't write or say anything negative to anyone; I always focus on my team and help everyone, especially since I usually play as an Off-Support or Hard Support because my preferred position of Hard Carry is already taken in 99% of the matches. I don't want to spend 30 minutes in the queue ¬¬'. I am consistently recognized as a "Featured Player" in 87% of my matches, and I am even the MvP in almost 35% of them. I NEVER receive any reports of any kind, yet my "Conduct" score keeps decreasing and moving without being able to increase. Sometimes, I receive +20 positive comments and no reports, but my "Conduct" score only goes up by 50 points or even drops by 100 points ¬¬'. It makes no sense at all.

To make matters worse, sometimes my "Conduct Summary" updates more than once in the same day without having played or even come close to 15 matches between summaries, and this is something you will see in some of the screenshots I will upload.

This is not normal, it makes no sense, and I request a review of my account. A review that Steam itself has already denied, attributing everything to the fact that "Behavior Summaries" are generated automatically... as if being "automated" makes it perfect and devoid of any issues. When did humans give so much power to technology that they don't even bother to check for irregularities? Have we gone mad, or stupid, or something worse... useless?

I want my account to be reviewed because what I'm experiencing is far from normal. And I want to point out that I have seen dozens of people facing the same issue, complaining since 2019 without receiving any help or support from Valve, which is lamentable for a company of its size.
